overall_assessment: Track 26 exhibits rigorous adherence to Searchright quality governance and non-negotiable architectural invariants. First, human-authority gates are deeply embedded in the finite-state machine: critical transitions (protocol approval, execution authorization, screening completion, reporting closeout, and living-review re-scoping) unconditionally require human identity and affirmative sign-off. Second, autonomous screening exclusion by agents is strictly prohibited: agent actors attempting to close FullTextComplete or emit Reported states are rejected with AssuranceError::AgentAuthorityDenied. Third, Hypothesis stateful property fuzzing over the searchright-mcp stdio binary (tests/test_mcp_authority_state_machine.py) confirms that unverified callers and autonomous agents cannot bypass authority checks, mutate review states, or record screening decisions without a valid protocol authority token. Fourth, PRISMA-S contracts are treated strictly as reporting standards rather than conduct mandates. Fifth, the schema migration registry operates completely fail-closed, blocking destructive changes, implicit write upgrades, or unmapped versions. Open maturity gates (Kani mathematical proofs, live Loom thread permutations, and persisted data migration drills) are honestly and explicitly documented without false promotion.
verified_invariants: PRISMA-S reporting contract: PRISMA-S is enforced as an auditable reporting contract and not mischaracterized as an autonomous conduct standard
no autonomous screening exclusion: automated agents cannot record screening exclusions or close screening stages without recorded human confirmation
fail-closed authority: MCP stdio server and assurance engine reject unauthenticated, unverified, or out-of-sequence lifecycle mutations
human-in-the-loop sign-off: critical lifecycle state transitions demand human actor classification and affirmative approval flags
safe schema migration: migration registry denies destructive migrations, forbids implicit write upgrades, and mandates backups and receipts
deterministic harness verification: all static and behavioral checks pass with zero unwrap/expect panic paths and complete error propagation
honest claim boundaries: source-verified claims are distinguished from formal mathematical proofs and production persisted data drills
